title: Discernment vs response bias in AI labels
why: Fixes measurement: computes sensitivity and criterion from AI and real post responses, and adds confidence ratings.

power_target.basis: Observed Automated Flagging effect 0.032 to 0.044 on total accuracy; H1 MDE at n=127/181 was 0.042; n=400/arm gives about 0.028 for SD 0.13.

rationale: Automated Flagging raised total accuracy by 4.4 points (95% CI [1.4, 7.3]), and some arms raised the share of AI posts identified, but the source reports only share-correct scores. Without per-post responses to both AI and real posts, we cannot tell better discernment from a greater tendency to answer 'AI'. This design computes d' and criterion and adds confidence ratings and a label-accuracy arm.
contribution: Separates true sensitivity from response bias for automated AI labels, and tests whether a stated label error rate changes either.
hypothesis: Automated Flagging raises d' relative to control; any increase in AI responses (a more liberal criterion) is separate from sensitivity, and the stated error rate reduces reliance on labels.
primary_outcome: d' computed from AI and real post responses (log-linear corrected), with criterion c as co-primary.
comparison: Each flagging arm vs control on d' and criterion; flagging vs flagging with error rate.
unresolved: The 24 image and video files and their labels must be supplied by the research team.
IRB approval number and compensation amount must be supplied by the research team.
label: Design advance

title: Label effect by label reliability and prior AI skill
why: Fixes the sample and missing-moderator causes by testing where the one robust effect holds.

power_target.basis: Observed Automated Flagging +0.032 raw; n=350/arm gives MDE about 0.03 at SD 0.13.

rationale: Automated Flagging was the one robust gain (+4.4 points, 95% CI [1.4, 7.3], p=0.004; control n=181 of 2,030 analysed), but the labels' accuracy was not varied and no moderator such as AI familiarity was tested. This design tests whether the benefit holds when labels are 95% versus 70% accurate, across AI familiarity levels, and for images versus videos.
contribution: Maps the conditions (label reliability, AI familiarity, media type) under which automated AI labels improve discernment on both AI and real posts.
hypothesis: Labels at 95% accuracy raise accuracy over control; labels at 70% accuracy raise it less or not at all, and may lower accuracy on posts the labels mislabel. The benefit is larger for low-familiarity respondents.
primary_outcome: Share of posts judged correctly, reported separately for AI posts and real posts, and by image versus video.
comparison: Each label arm versus control; 95% versus 70% accuracy; interaction with ai_scale tercile and with media type.
unresolved: The research team must supply the image and video files and the label overlays.
IRB approval number and participant compensation must be supplied.
The panel's ability to stratify on ai_scale before randomisation must be confirmed.
label: Generalizability

title: Platform labels vs user training head to head
why: Fixes design and power: contrasts only the best-supported system arm with the best user-side arm in a focused comparison.

power_target.basis: Observed Guide-vs-control raw difference 0.006 and adjusted 0.047; size to detect a 0.03 label-vs-guide gap (H1 SD about 0.13).

rationale: In the source study only Automated Flagging moved accuracy (+4.4 points, 95% CI [1.4, 7.3]), while the AI Literacy Guide was borderline and model-dependent (adjusted +4.7, raw difference about 0.006). Arms were heterogeneous and some had only 78-102 respondents, so the i-frame vs s-frame debate was not settled. This design compares only the best system arm with the best user arm, plus their combination, with per-post responses and a 1-week follow-up.
contribution: A focused, adequately powered test of whether system-supplied labels outperform user training, and whether the two add up, using per-post responses so discernment can be separated from response bias.
hypothesis: H1 (s-frame): Automated Flagging yields higher total accuracy than the AI Literacy Guide. H2: the combined arm exceeds either single arm (additive effects). Rival (i-frame): the Guide matches labels, particularly at 1 week.
primary_outcome: Total accuracy (share of 24 posts judged correctly) at wave 1, contrast labels vs guide.
comparison: Pre-registered: Labels vs Guide. Then Both vs each single arm, and each arm vs control. Secondary: accuracy on AI posts and real posts, and wave 2 (1 week) accuracy.
unresolved: The actual media files, labels and guide must be supplied by the research team.
IRB approval number and compensation need to be set.
The wave 2 invitation and recontact procedure must be built.
label: Theoretical debate
